title: Deep learning identifies Alzheimer's disease progression patterns, with Mendelian randomization
summary: A deep learning model jointly predicted time-to-conversion and clustered subgroups along the cognitively normal to MCI to AD dementia trajectory in ADNI (1370 participants). The patterns had different progression rates, for example CN to MCI hazard ratio 3.51, and were externally validated in AIBL (233 participants); Mendelian randomization was used for causal inference. External subgroups are small, covariates were merged and imputed, and an earlier SSRN preprint (2023-07-03) was not checked, so an earlier public date is possible.
ai_technology: Deep learning model for joint time-to-conversion prediction and clustering

evidence.tested: ADNI (1370) design and validation, AIBL (233) external validation and Mendelian randomization.
evidence.unknown: Clinical validity of the patterns; the earlier preprint version was not checked.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning clustered progression subgroups and predicted time-to-conversion.
